$Comment: The per-kit mapping import_kit.py reads: which vanilla cave-node graph a kit's pieces come from, which prefab pools it
imports, how its pools are named, tagged and given roles, and how its door classes are named.
Graph: folders under CaveRoot whose .node.json files are the kit's graph. Pools: prefab-name prefixes to import (a pool
outside them is skipped, and so is every join to it). PieceRoot: the prefix cut from a pool to make the piece name in
Zc_Kit_<Kit>_<Piece>. Tags: the engine's own Tags map (key to values) on every room, Kit naming the kit; TagRules add
values by pool prefix (Section: a level or part of the kit), and a Cap takes, key by key, every value of the rooms
whose doors it can close. The engine reads a map as each key, each value and each Key=Value, so a plan filters with
Kit=Stone or Section=Tomb. Roles: the pool's folder path, matched on
its longest dotted suffix. Kinds: a door class (the doors vanilla's graph joins, closed under joining) takes the Kind
of the first rule naming a pool one of its doors sits on; a class no rule names takes Default. ClipDepth: how far
(in blocks) a room's blocks may stand proud of a doorway's wall and be left out of its Box, so the doorway sits on
the Box's face; a room whose doorway stays inside its Box is not imported (PD1's box test could never join it).
Fill: the block written as every room's Fill. Vanilla pastes these pieces into solid rock, and the painter fills the
cells a piece leaves unlisted inside its Box with it. Rock_Stone for the Stone and Cursed Crypt kits: the most common
solid block across the Cursed Crypt's pieces (about twice the next), the most common block facing the Stone kit's
carved air (just ahead of Rock_Quartzite), and the natural rock of the zone vanilla digs both into. FillRules give a
pool prefix its own Fill, the first rule naming the pool winning. CaveRoot: the folder a kit's Graph folders and
node names are under; a kit may name its own (a graph in another zone), else this one. Plugs: true gives every
door Kind no imported Cap closes a plug cap, Zc_Kit_<Kit>_Plug[_<Kind>]: PlugPrefab (vanilla's empty prefab) over a
slab Box one block deep across the widest doorway of the Kind, filled with Fill at paint time. Vanilla digs these
kits into rock, so a doorway its graph leaves open runs into rock, and the plug is that rock, shaped like the Stone
kit's own Walls caps.
Not imported: Cursed.Transition_Cursed.Stairs. Its West and South doors sit inside its own Box (the stair's
upper body stands over them), so no neighbour or cap could meet them. It was vanilla's only join between the
Cursed section (Kind Cursed_Crypt) and the Tomb section (Kind Cursed_Crypt_Tomb), so a script-built adapter
room (PD7) must make that join: a door of each Kind.
Cursed_Crypt.Label: the Cursed Crypt

$Comment: Vanilla's graph has two stages: the ruins (Stage_2: the C_Large and C_Small corridors, the Rooms and the
Stairs_Normal stair) and the Structured_Cave below (Stage_3), joined by Rooms.End's stair down. The Entrance
pieces are surface buildings, not rooms, so they are left out as the other kits leave theirs. Fill follows the
section: Rock_Quartzite is the most common solid block across the ruins' pieces (about five times Rock_Stone),
Rock_Stone across the Structured_Cave's (about seventeen times the next). The graph ships a wall cap for the
ruins (C_Small.End) but none for the Structured_Cave, so the kit takes plugs.
Magic_Ruins.Label: the Magic Ruins

$Comment: Vanilla's Shale dungeon graph is Zone 3's (Zone3_Tier1/Cave/Dungeons; the Tier2 and Tier3 copies differ only
in their Mask file), so this kit names its own CaveRoot. Its Room_Small and Room_Medium pools serve all three
levels and Room_Large the third, so they carry those levels' Section values. Its OffGrid corridors are named
in the graph under Dungeon.Shale.System_2, a folder that holds none, so vanilla pastes nothing there and they
are left out. Fill is Rock_Shale, the most common solid block across its pieces and the zone's own rock. The
graph ships no wall cap at all (its open doorways end in the zone's rock), so the kit takes plugs. Its rooms
have one door each (side rooms off the tunnels), and Corridors_Drop is a dead end whose floor falls away.
Shale.Label: the Shale mines
